notes: Ethereum mainnet (chainId 1). TOKEN: NUKE is a plain OpenZeppelin ERC-20 (18 decimals, no constructor args, no custom logic or fees) whose constructor mints the whole 1e27-unit supply to its deployer, the launch factory, which seeds the pool and distributes the swarm allocation. CONSTRUCTOR ARGS of NUKEHook, in declaration order: IPoolManager $poolManager (the chain's Uniswap v4 PoolManager; on mainnet 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90) and address $token (the NUKE the factory deploys just before the hook). The constructor requires both to have code and derives the sorted NUKE/IMD pool key itself. IMD (the paired currency) and the DEAD burn destination are compile-time constants, so there is no owner, factory, recipient or setter argument and no $owner/$factory placeholder applies. PERMISSION BITS, as returned by getHookPermissions(): beforeInitialize (bit 13, 0x2000), beforeSwap (bit 7, 0x80), afterSwap (bit 6, 0x40) and afterSwapReturnDelta (bit 2, 0x4); every other flag, including beforeSwapReturnDelta, is false. The hook itself (no wrapper or proxy) must be CREATE2-deployed at an address with address & 0x3fff == 0x20c4 (8388); the constructor validates this and reverts otherwise. Every callback and unlockCallback accepts only the PoolManager. beforeInitialize accepts exactly one pool, once: the sorted NUKE/IMD key with the listed static LP fee 12500, tickSpacing 60 and this hook, from any initializer (the launch factory); it records the opening sqrtPriceX96 as the first reference observation and starts the first one-hour batch interval. FEES: the pool's static 1.25% LP fee (12500) is untouched (no dynamic-fee flag, no updateDynamicLPFee, no override). beforeSwap returns a zero BeforeSwapDelta and zero LP override and only rejects requests whose |amountSpecified| plus its 1% fee cannot fit int256 (UnrepresentableFee); real swaps never revert in the hook. afterSwap charges the 100 bps hook fee as floor(|unspecified BalanceDelta| / 100) on what actually filled, returned as a positive afterSwapReturnDelta on the unspecified currency (NUKE output on an exact-input buy, IMD output on an exact-input sell, IMD input on an exact-output buy, NUKE input on an exact-output sell) and minted to the hook as an ERC-6909 claim: nothing is transferred or spent inside a swap, no fee is reserved in beforeSwap, and a price-limited partial fill pays only on the filled amount. Swaps the hook starts itself pay no hook fee. sweep(), callable by anyone, redeems NUKE claims and sends all NUKE the hook holds to DEAD. executeBatch(), callable by anyone in its own transaction (refused while the PoolManager is unlocked), runs at most once per 3600 s: it spends up to 25% of pending() IMD as an exact-input swap through PoolManager.unlock/swap with a sqrtPriceLimit 300 bps beyond the stricter of referencePrice() (time-weighted mean observed tick of the last completed launch-aligned hour) and the executable spot, accepts partial fills (unspent IMD stays pending, so it cannot deadlock), has no minimum-output check, and sends all bought NUKE to DEAD; zero-output batches roll back and, like fills below 1% of the budget, leave the interval open. Observations are the price at which 0.25% of the manager's NUKE is purchasable, found by walking initialized ticks; empty regions and dust positions are not adopted, and each observation is clamped to at most 2000 ticks below the previous hour's mean. Views: pending(), pendingBurn(), lastBatch(), referencePrice(), observedTick(), askPrice(), batchPriceLimit(). pool.initialPrice is provenance only (1:1 sqrtPriceX96); the factory sets the economic opening price. No owner, setters, proxy, selfdestruct, delegatecall or upgradeability; all parameters are immutable constants.
